- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often overshoot after recent spikes, then sharply correct downward — suggest dampening response to short-term volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate gradual pullback after peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in high volatility periods (e.g., 2024-05-20, 2024-08-16) — reduce forecast magnitude when history shows erratic swings.
- Lagged corrections are common: model reacts to recent history but misses 1–2 day lag in true price shifts.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5–7 days are rising, don’t assume continuation; instead, model should adjust downward if volatility is high or trend is flattening.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term downward drift — consider incorporating moving average or trend filter to reduce overconfidence in short-term momentum.
